scope: Bounded HTML tooltip observation and Fara page-reading integration, following real MCP/browser capability probes
productionChanges: Preserve an optional website-declared HTML tooltip separately on each rendered text record. Keep original captions, control labels and rendered-text answer verification unchanged.
Use composed ancestors to find the applicable title, stop inheritance at an explicit empty title, and exclude hidden/unrendered/control/editor text through the existing text admission rules.
Limit individual metadata to 2048 UTF-8 bytes, guard oversized raw attributes before encoding, include metadata in the total 65536-byte snapshot limit, and mark omitted data as truncated.

Include clearly labeled Website tooltip data in the existing 4096-byte Fara page-reading projection. Snapshot serialization and validation include the metadata, so a changed tooltip invalidates the old read.
findings: The public page opens while document.readyState is interactive. Immediate snapshot reads return stale; a bounded test-only wait for complete obtains valid existing page evidence. No production readiness guard was weakened, and production readiness handling remains open.
The loaded page renders 2 weeks ago in an open shadow tree while its HTML title supplies the exact publication date. Native element innerText alone misses the shadow caption.

The pinned real MCP get_ui_tree and broad find_elements responses exceed the current structured-output budget and are omitted. A limit-12 query returns 12 records with limit_reached=true, so it is explicitly partial. A query using the actual observed time caption finds zero AXStaticText matches. These probes do not prove every possible MCP query is incapable of reading the date.

The failing native regression omitted tooltips for ordinary time/text and shadow content. The repaired workflow and metadata inheritance, exclusion, Unicode, per-item/aggregate bounds and changed-tooltip checks pass.

A broader existing test expected pageChanged for a stale prepared link. The unchanged pre-existing openObservedDestination validation maps an invalid link reply to linkNavigationUnavailable. Corrected only that expected error; stale evidence rejection, no effect callback and zero destination requests remain asserted. Baseline error mapping was verified by source inspection, not a separate baseline execution.

The real production reader now includes the correct observed publication tooltip in 2626 bytes in 4.32 seconds, with no inference or mutation ledger. This is a capability probe with scripted reader selection, not autonomous task acceptance.

The unchanged real natural-language task still fails after 98.99 seconds. Ten model replies are captured; the last is a syntactically valid visit_url request for view-source:https://github.com/apple/swift-nio/releases/tag/2.102.0. The current strict decoder rejects that scheme as invalidResponse before navigation. The model never invokes page reading.
All 13 selected methods pass on the final build with no skips. The real public run and final regression bundle retain the existing UI-unresponsiveness warning.
remainingWork: Return bounded unsupported-navigation feedback to the actor without ever navigating a rejected scheme; prove that it can select the existing page reader and complete the unchanged task. Preserve strict malformed-response checks, ownership, cancellation and no-effect guarantees.
Qualify production initial-page readiness without relying on model startup latency.
General tool selection, real provider/phone controls, native/cross-app coverage, whole-Mac 12 GB/heat and full production acceptance remain open.
limitations: MCP priority, browser model selection, worker limit, and installed application are unchanged.
The public capability probe uses a test-owned browser and explicit page readiness wait. Only the last full task uses actual model decisions.
The failed full task is diagnostic HostSession composition with a normal runtime/loader plus an explicit response observer and isolated browser/task journals.
Tooltip data is website content, not trusted instruction or proof of another requested result. Native input authorization remains separate.
Source hashes bind the final passing build and full-model trial. Earlier probe source varied; their original logs/results remain retained.
